heading: G8_How To Use Adjectives vs Adverbs

topics.heading: How To Use Adjectives vs Adverbs

question: Choose the best option to complete the sentence correctly.
The musician played the piece so ___ that even the critics sat in stunned silence.
Identify whether the underlined word is an adjective or an adverb.
They were slow as they carefully went through the dense fog.
Which sentence uses an adverb where an adjective should be used?

options.text: He became quickly frustrated with the delay.
She looks tired after the journey.
The room smelled fresh after the cleaning.

question: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
The storm grew ___ as it moved toward the coastline.
Which sentence is grammatically correct and uses the adjective/adverb correctly?

options.text: She spoke soft to avoid waking the baby.
He felt nervously before entering the stage.
The lake looked still under the moonlight.

question: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The journalist wrote so ___ that even complex issues became understandable to the average reader.
Identify the underlined word:
The children sat quietly as the teacher entered the room.
Which sentence uses an adjective <u>incorrectly</u> in place of an adverb?

options.text: She looked calm despite the chaos.
He worked efficient during the crisis.
That dog smells awful after the rain.

question: Choose the word that best fits the sentence <u>meaningfully and grammatically.</u>
The coach spoke ___ to motivate the losing team.
Which sentence contains correct usage of an adverb/adjective?

options.text: The soup smells delicious as it simmers.
The flowers smell fragrantly in the morning.
The fabric feels smoothly on the skin.
The cake tastes sweetly with every bite.

question: Choose the correct option to complete the sentence.
The director was ___ upset by the actor’s repeated mistakes during the shoot.
Identify the underlined word:
He arrived late to the ceremony and missed the opening speech.
Which of the following sentences contains incorrect usage of an adverb in place of an adjective?

options.text: The landscape looks beautifully at sunset.
The air feels chilly in the morning.
The engine sounds rough after starting.
Her voice seems tired from overuse.

question: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
The rescue team worked ___ to locate the missing hikers before nightfall.
Which sentence is grammatically correct and uses the adverb/adjective appropriately?

options.text: She sounded angrily when discussing the issue.
He acted strange after receiving the news.
They remained hopeful despite the odds.
The team played skillful throughout the game.
